plan.topic: Didn't hear the second click on your tirzepatide single-dose pen? What the Instructions for Use say the clicks mean
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Tirzepatide pen: didn't hear the second click? Here's what the pen guide says.' By 6 s, paraphrase or quote the US single-dose pen IFU: hold for up to 10 seconds; first click = started, second loud click = complete; a softer click may come first; keep the pen on the skin until the second loud click. Then the check the IFU gives: the gray plunger being visible means the dose was delivered. If you can't see it, follow the leaflet's printed instruction and contact the number in your IFU or your healthcare provider. Don't inject again on your own. Scope card: 'US single-dose pen only. KwikPens and vials work differently. Check the leaflet in your box.' Optional stat card: 'Zepbound label (weight-management trials): injection-site reactions 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo.' Closing in 11-16 order: the scoped don't-stop/change line, 'Not personal advice', the full prescriber line, the Exp F line, then 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'
plan.why: A visible pen moment in the slot where our pen and injection-site Shorts win (pen blood 111, injection site 254 and 202). It's a new question, and it feeds the Pen how-to long video. | fact-check: Real 'is this normal?' moment, and the IFU answers it directly. The Zepbound single-dose pen IFU (https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf) says to press and hold for up to 10 seconds. The first click means the injection started, the second click means it's complete, and a soft click may come before the second loud click. It also says not to remove the pen until the second loud click, that the gray plunger being visible confirms the dose was delivered, and that if you don't see the gray plunger you should contact Lilly at 1-800-545-5979. The 'what to do if unsure' answer is therefore the gray-plunger check plus the IFU's own contact instruction. Don't make the main instruction 'contact your pharmacist or prescriber', though adding healthcare provider as a second option is fine. Never suggest injecting again. Fixes: (a) 'US' scope must be on screen, because UK/AU viewers mostly have the Mounjaro KwikPen, which works differently, and a US KwikPen for Zepbound now exists too. (b) The 6–8% vs about 2% injection-site figure comes from the Zepbound label's weight-management trials. Name that source and population on the stat card ('Zepbound label, weight-management trials'), or drop the line. Don't present it as true for every user of this pen, because Mounjaro's label has different rates. (c) Quote the IFU only if the IFU URL itself loads. The PI is not the IFU.

factcheck.summary:
Passes with three minor fixes. The cited source is Lilly's US Zepbound single-dose pen Instructions for Use (pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf). The URL loads as a real 300 KB PDF, but the fetch tool couldn't read its text. I checked its content through a search summary that attributes these points to the same file, rather than by reading the PDF myself. They match every claim in the script:
- Press and hold for up to 10 seconds.
- The first click means the injection has started; the second click means it's complete.
- Some people hear a soft click right before the second loud click.
- Don't take the pen off your skin until the second loud click.
- If the gray plunger is visible, the dose was delivered.
- If you don't see the gray plunger, contact Lilly at 1-800-Lilly-Rx.

The script paraphrases all of this and quotes nothing.

What's already right:
- The channel safety lines ("Don't inject again on your own", "or your healthcare provider") are correctly not credited to the IFU.
- The scope card in s6 stops UK and AU KwikPen users from applying US autoinjector instructions to their pens.
- The safety close and the Exp F and closing lines are correct for content dated 2026-11-16.
- Spoken words come to about 156, under the 160 limit.
- The hook pays off, and nothing is dosing, switching or stopping advice.

The three minor fixes are below: muted-viewer scope on the s1 opening card, the source entry's missing revised date, and a keyword and naming alignment between Mounjaro and Zepbound.

issues.claim: Tirzepatide pen: didn't hear second click?
issues.problem: With the sound off, viewers see 'Tirzepatide pen' with no scope, and the 'US single-dose pen' limit doesn't appear until s2. Under the playbook's muted-viewer rule, on-screen text should keep the scope. The phrase is also missing 'the'.
issues.fix: Change on_screen_text to: "Tirzepatide US single-dose pen: didn't hear the second click?"

issues.problem: The playbook says every source entry needs its live revised date, not just an access date. The fetch tool couldn't read the IFU PDF's text, so I couldn't take the revised date from the file.
issues.fix: Open the PDF, read the 'Revised: MM/YYYY' line on its last page, and set year to "Revised [MM/YYYY]; accessed 2026-11-16". If you can't read the date, keep "Accessed 2026-11-16" and say so in the post notes.

issues.claim: target_keyword 'mounjaro pen didn't click'; narration cites only the Zepbound single-dose pen guide
issues.problem: The target keyword is about Mounjaro, but the only source is the Zepbound IFU. In the US, Mounjaro also comes in a single-dose autoinjector. That pen is built the same way, but this script doesn't cite its IFU. The video stays accurate because s2 says 'Zepbound's' and s6 limits the scope. The packaging, though, must not say the Mounjaro pen guide was checked.
issues.fix: Either add the Mounjaro US single-dose pen IFU as a separate source with its own URL, or keep the script as it is and tell packaging not to use #Mounjaro or 'Mounjaro pen guide' wording. Use 'tirzepatide (Zepbound) US single-dose pen' in the title and description.
